Re: Appeal of denial for partial knee replacement, CPT 27446

Dear Wellpoint Appeals Reviewer:

I appeal the denial of prior authorization for partial knee replacement, CPT 27446. The notice dated August 25, 2026, identifies insufficient documentation of conservative treatment as the basis for denial.

The clinical records demonstrate an adequate and unsuccessful course of conservative treatment:

- I have experienced 14 months of progressive knee pain that has not been relieved by rest.
- I used NSAIDs for six months, with inadequate relief.
- I received a corticosteroid injection on May 1, 2026. It provided only four weeks of partial relief.
- I completed 12 weeks of supervised physical therapy from April 22, 2026, through July 15, 2026, totaling 20 visits. The physical therapy discharge note documents completion of this treatment, including quadriceps strengthening and range-of-motion work.
- Despite these measures, I continue to have substantial pain and functional impairment. I cannot climb stairs without assistance and wake three to four times each night because of pain.

The objective findings support the need for surgery:

- MRI on July 10, 2026, showed full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition.
- The MRI documented Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medial disease.
- Examination showed positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain.

The record also documents appropriate surgical candidacy factors. There is no active infection or untreated substance use. BMI is 29, and I am a nonsmoker. Duval, MD, orthopedic surgeon, has requested the procedure based on the persistent symptoms, failed conservative treatment, objective imaging, and significant functional limitations.

Accordingly, the submitted records directly address the stated concern regarding conservative treatment. They document medication therapy, injection treatment, and a completed supervised physical-therapy course, followed by persistent pain and disability. I request that Wellpoint overturn the denial and approve CPT 27446.

If Wellpoint maintains the denial, please provide the exact medical policy or clinical-review guideline applied to this request, including its title, policy or guideline number, version or effective date, the complete medical-necessity criteria used, and the clinical records relied upon in the determination. The applicable policy or clinical-review criteria were not provided with the notice and were not publicly retrievable, so this letter does not quote or assume any plan policy language.

Please also confirm receipt of this appeal and provide the appeal determination in writing. The notice identifies February 21, 2027, as the appeal deadline.

Sincerely,

Morgan Iverson
